newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end lower on U.S. weakness.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end lower on U.S. weakness.

text.p: * Toronto stocks lost 27.22 points in quiet trading on Tuesday, weighted down by falling U.S. markets and year-end profit-taking in large capitalization companies.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 101.10 to 6448.27, hurt by a weak bond market.
"Other than that, I think there's some profit-taking after some increases in stock prices in Canada yesterday," Ketchen said.

On Monday, the TSE 300 leaped ahead 51.64 points, led by large capitalization issues. But on Tuesday, several large-cap issues ended down, with Seagram Co Ltd losing C$2.35 to close at C$54.25, Placer Dome Inc off C$0.85 to end at C$30.05 and BCE Inc dropping 0.85 to C$65.30.
Among the 14 subindices, consumer products lost the most, dropping 2.13 percent, followed by conglomerates, which slid 1.59 percent.

While the market dropped on Tuesday, it made substantial gains on the year. The TSE 300 rose 25.74 percent in 1996, up 1213.49 points from last year's close at 4713.54. The 1996 total trading value was about C$301 billion, almost C$100 billion more than in 1995.
"That's not bad. I'll take it. I hope we can duplicate it next year, which I'm assuming here in Canada we can do," Ketchen said.
